subject: Reserved queue deposit vs OEM credit swap — procurement cadence and fallback lane
messages:
From: Acme AI procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Reserved capacity ask for Q4 onboarding

Kim —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We need to lock a two-phase dedicated pool for our Q4 onramp: 40 A100-equivalent slots for pilot (Nov), scaling to 160 by Jan. Procurement is trying to reconcile two parallel asks from engineering: a) commit to a reserved-queue deposit with Redwood (to guarantee warm capacity) and b) pursue OEM credit terms to accelerate on-prem hardware if cloud lead times slip.

Our questions: which approach gives the strongest SLA guarantee by early Nov, and what are the cutover mechanics if we start in Redwood Hosted/Dedicated and then migrate some workloads to OEM on-prem? We have a procurement window that closes Oct 7, so we need clear numbers/lead times and a recommendation.

Attached: Acme_proposal_v3.pdf — outline of forecast and expected QPS.

Procurement
Acme AI

Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask for Q4 onboarding

Thanks — looping in Karthik (capacity/product) and Ben (procurement/commercial).

Short answer up front: a reserved Redwood Dedicated commitment is the fastest path to hard SLOs and predictable latency for Nov. OEM credits can accelerate on-prem cadence but typically add 8–14 weeks from order to rack-ready depending on SKU and customs. We can build a hybrid plan: reserve a minimal warm pool with us for Nov (pilot) and run a parallel OEM credit negotiation to backfill peak demand in Jan. If OEM can offer delivery within 8 weeks and provide a credit that nets out of the Redwood reserved commitment, that could be an optional swap.

Ask to Acme: send a prioritized SKU list (GPU/CPU/memory targets) and whether you need physical colocation or an OEM-managed appliance. Ben — can you outline our standard reserved deposit terms and whether we can structure a conditional credit holdback to accommodate an OEM swap?

Kim
Director, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference

Subject: FW: Reserved capacity ask for Q4 onboarding — lead times & credit swap feasibility

Hi OEMCo / CloudScale — forwarding a forecast from Acme AI. They want a guaranteed minimum pool for Nov and are open to OEM credit if on-prem can arrive fast enough. Two quick asks:
1) OEMCo: realistic lead time range today for the following SKU bundles if order placed Oct 1: 40x A100-equivalent (pilot) and 160x (full); include logistics customs cushion for US East deployments.
2) CloudScale: what's your fastest reservable private pool for Nov 1 start (minimum duration 90 days)? Can you provide a short term (30–60 day) bridge with guaranteed warm capacity and a deposit schedule?

We may propose a commercial construct: Redwood reserves a pilot pool with Acme (deposit), OEMCo holds credit equivalent that can be applied within 90 days if delivered; if OEM delivery misses the agreed SLA, credits expire and Redwood retains deposit. If OEM delivers early, Acme can request a prorated refund/credit against the Redwood commitment. Is that operationally possible on your side?

Thanks — Ben

Ben / Kimberly —

Thanks for the intro. Current ballpark lead times for A100-class racks to US East: 6–10 weeks from PO receipt (factory lead 4–6 weeks + transit/clearing 2–4 weeks). For the 40-unit pilot, we can prioritize a partial shipment in ~5–6 weeks if you accept mixed-shipment staging — smaller form factors first, full rack assembly follows. For 160 units, realistic end-to-end is 10–14 weeks.

On credits: we can support an OEM credit note equal to a percent of list value, issued once the PO is accepted. We can also reserve inventory against a refundable good-faith deposit (subject to an MOU). Practical constraints: credit issuance requires a signed master purchase agreement and a 10% deposit on our side to hold SKU allocations. Customs/regulatory hold-ups are the largest variance — heavy-duty GPUs often get flagged for export compliance checks that add 5–12 business days.

I'll attach a template quote and a draft MOU for the credit hold. If Redwood wants to be the counterparty for the credit swap construct, we can accept Redwood as the administrative recipient of the deposit.

Regards,
Marcel Duarte
Head, Customer Programs — OEMCo

Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Summary & ask — reserve-then-swap fallback plan (Acme / OEMCo)

Team — quick summary and proposed action items so procurement window (Oct 7) can close with clarity.

Summary:
- For a guaranteed Nov pilot start, Redwood can offer a 45-slot warm pool (we'll size to Acme's pilot QPS) with a refundable deposit structure: 20% upfront, 30% due at go-live, remainder amortized over the term. That pool gives explicit latency SLOs and priority routing.
- OEMCo estimates: pilot partial shipment in 5–6 weeks from PO; full 160-unit fulfillment ~10–14 weeks. Credit note and inventory reservation available with a 10% OEM deposit against an MOU.
- Proposed commercial construct (fallback lane): Acme signs Redwood reserved commitment for Nov (minimal pilot). OEMCo and Acme execute an MOU for credit reservation. If OEMCo delivers within 60 days of PO, Acme may elect to swap up to X% of the reserved slots and receive a prorated credit from Redwood. If OEMCo misses the 60-day SLA, OEM credit is void and Redwood retains deposit to cover committed capacity.

Action items:
1) Acme — confirm SKU priority list and whether OEM on-prem must be colocation or appliance (deadline: Oct 4).
2) Ben / Redwood legal (Laura) — can you draft the conditional credit holdback term-sheet (I attached a starter: reserved-queue-term-sheet.docx) and an execution timeline? (deadline: Oct 3).
3) OEMCo (Marcel) — please confirm the 5–6 / 10–14 week windows in writing and flag any export/customs risk based on Acme's target data centre region.
4) CloudScale — confirm short-term private pool availability and deposit schedule for a Nov 1 pilot (deadline: Sep 30 EOD).

I'll run the draft term-sheet with our legal and share a DocuSign link once Ben/Laura confirm conventions. Thanks everyone — this keeps Acme's Nov onboarding possible while buying time for OEM delivery.

Kim
Director, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference
